name: Iraq
headline: Iraq: −0.4% growth in 2025, 0.3% inflation, debt 53% of GDP
sections: Iraq is a $264 billion economy (2025), the world's 54th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew −0.4% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $14K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 4.0% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 0.3% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.0% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 15.5% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 32.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 53% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 73% in 2020. The general government balance is −6.2% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −3.8% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 77% of GDP (2024), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were −3.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 73% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 72.4 years (2024). Population: 45.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
